stores.name: The Meat Hook
stores.notes: OSM's address (100 Frost St) is outdated. The Meat Hook originally operated out of the back of The Brooklyn Kitchen at 100 Frost St starting in 2009, then relocated to its own space at 397 Graham Ave (at Jackson St) in February 2016, where it remains. Could not access Yelp review text directly (blocked) so no sentiments included despite the store having many reviews.

stores.name: C-Town

sentiments.text: One reviewer said the produce is better than Whole Foods, Key Food, Union Market, and Fairway, and is always fresh and rotated.
Another reviewer called it at least half the price of Whole Foods or Fairway.
A different reviewer found it overpriced compared to Foodtown next door, and mentioned expired food on shelves.

stores.notes: Reviews are mixed: praise for produce quality and price vs. complaints about cashier attitude and expired items.

stores.name: Southside Food Plaza
stores.notes: OSM listed the address as 430 Bedford Ave; Yelp and the NYS food-store registry both give 428 Bedford Ave, likely the same building. No concrete review text found, only directory-style descriptions ('great selection', 'competitive prices') that aren't attributable to a specific review, so left out of sentiments.

stores.name: Rachel's Garden

sentiments.text: Reviewers note it's open 24 hours with fresh fruit and Polish imports at reasonable prices, though some reported moldy produce and stale items.

stores.notes: There's a separate, now-CLOSED Yelp listing for 'Rachel's Garden' at 122 Nassau Ave (a few doors down) — likely a prior location or an OSM/Yelp duplicate. This entry is for the currently active 116 Nassau Ave store, which has a 2.5-star average on Yelp.

stores.name: Market on Kent
stores.notes: Despite the name, the store's address is 921 Manhattan Ave, at the corner of Manhattan Ave and Kent St (not on Kent Ave itself). No concrete review quotes found.

stores.name: Foodtown

sentiments.text: Neighbors describe the staff as very friendly and helpful, with good selection, fresh produce, and a recently renovated store.
Reviewers mention the large deli counter is useful for lunch on the go or bigger catering orders.

stores.notes: Reviews found were consistently positive; owned by Nasri Abed per one directory listing.

stores.name: Shop Fair
stores.notes: Address inferred from an 'Shop Fair of Williamsburg' business listing at 385 Broadway (not independently confirmed against the store's own signage/site — no official website found). Found no specialty-item or review information beyond bare directory listings. Given the chain also has several unrelated Shop Fair locations elsewhere in Brooklyn (Church Ave, Livonia Ave, Fulton St), treat this address with some caution.

sentiments.text: Described as a reliable, well-stocked, clean, and friendly neighborhood market with good produce, salads, and deli items, and competitive sale prices.
One December 2024 review noted the produce section is small and some items, like fresh string beans, were hard to find.

stores.name: C-Town
stores.notes: Could not find store-specific reviews for this Manhattan Ave (Greenpoint) location — a directory listing turned up with zero reviews. specialtyItems kept generic since nothing store-specific was verifiable; avoided guessing based on the chain's reputation at other locations.

stores.name: Kahan's Food Mart
stores.notes: No dedicated website found for this location. Some search results surfaced reviews for the unrelated 'Kahan's Superette' in Crown Heights (317 Kingston Ave) — a different business under a similar name — so those were not used here.

stores.name: Schwartz Supermarket

sentiments.text: Described as having a quiet atmosphere with a varied kosher product selection, with prices ranked among the best in town.

stores.notes: OSM listed the address as 118 Lee Ave; multiple sources (Waze, business directories, the store's own site) confirm 120 Lee Ave.

stores.name: Bonny Grocert
bestBuys: beer selection (advertised as the biggest in Williamsburg)
stores.notes: OSM tags this as a greengrocer, but available info (business's own marketing, directory listings) describes it as a Dominican-owned family bodega/deli operating since 1986, known for its beer selection and deli sandwiches — not primarily a produce shop. No dedicated website found; social presence is on Facebook/TikTok/Instagram.

stores.name: Bravo

sentiments.text: One reviewer called it a great neighborhood spot, except when turned away near closing time.
Another reviewer warned to never buy the produce there and to check expiration dates on most items.
A different reviewer called it an excellent, convenient supermarket with professional and friendly customer service.

stores.notes: Reviews are notably mixed on freshness/quality control vs. convenience and service.

stores.name: Tokyo Mart
specialtyItems: Japan-exclusive snacks (e.g. matcha and strawberry Kit-Kats)

sentiments.text: Customers describe it as an authentic Japanese grocery with a nostalgic feel, and praise thoughtful staff who often add complimentary items at checkout.

stores.notes: OSM had no address; store opened at 517 Grand St in 2023, run by owner Ken and his brothers Tony and Johnny. No official standalone website found (listed on DoorDash/Grubhub/Uber Eats for delivery).

stores.name: MOORE GOURMET DELI INC
stores.notes: Functions primarily as a deli/bodega (drinks, snacks, pantry goods, prepared food, alcohol) rather than a full grocery store, based on delivery-app listings (DoorDash, Grubhub, Seamless, Postmates). No dedicated website found and no real review text located, only a 4.5-star aggregate rating with no visible text.

stores.name: Met Foodmarket

sentiments.text: One reviewer called it 'one of the most grocery-store grocery stores I've ever been in,' meant endearingly, and 'a great, big, friendly grocery store.'
Another reviewer said the produce and cut fruit are never fresh, and that meat purchased there once smelled and tasted off.
A different reviewer said the store is 'ok' overall but staff rarely offer a 'thank you' or eye contact.

stores.notes: Operates as 'Met Foodmarkets of Greenpoint,' part of the independently-owned Met Foodmarkets banner. Reviews are mixed on freshness and staff friendliness.

stores.name: Associated Supermarket

sentiments.text: Shoppers say the store leans into Eastern European and Polish staples, with a good variety at reasonable prices for authentic regional foods.

stores.notes: Part of the Associated Supermarkets co-op banner; website/flyer links are the chain's, filtered to this store's circular. No address was missing from OSM (confirmed correct).

stores.name: Mazur Meat Market

sentiments.text: One regular called it "my favorite Polish meat market, good quality and products," and another praised the kielbasa as the best around.
A few reviewers describe the shop as dated and report being overcharged at the register without a receipt.

stores.notes: No official website found; Yelp rating is mixed (around 2.5 stars) despite positive comments about the kielbasa specifically.

stores.name: Whole Foods Market

sentiments.text: Reviewers like the prepared-food selection (e.g. Beecher's frozen pasta) and local-brand offerings like Roberta's.
Some reviewers say the store is understaffed and that produce quality has slipped, with reports of soggy or spoiled lettuce.

stores.notes: Address and website were already correct from OSM.

stores.name: Brooklyn Harvest Market

sentiments.text: Shoppers highlight the well-curated produce, a strong vegetarian/vegan selection, and friendly, helpful cashiers.
Several note prices run higher than a typical supermarket.

stores.notes: Note there is a separate Brooklyn Harvest Market location at 25 N 5th St — this entry is specifically the Union Ave store.

stores.name: The Meat Hook
stores.notes: OSM record had no address; the given coordinates (40.7167566, -73.9449541) actually correspond to the shop's former location at 100 Frost St, which has since closed. The Meat Hook's current Williamsburg location is 397 Graham Ave (they also have Carroll Gardens and Hudson, NY locations) — used the current address here since the old one no longer operates. Old website the-meathook.com now resolves via themeathook.com.

stores.name: Sunac Natural Foods

sentiments.text: Regulars call it their go-to for fresh, healthy food in Williamsburg, citing consistently excellent quality and a strong prepared-foods section.
Some say it's one of the pricier options in the area and that they still need a regular grocery store for basics.

stores.notes: 3.9 stars from 234+ Yelp reviews as of last check.

stores.name: Ozzie's Fresh Market
stores.notes: OSM name had a typo ("Ozzie;s Fresh Marker") and no address — corrected name and added address found via Yelp/Waze/Facebook. It appears to operate under/affiliated with the Associated banner, which is likely why shopassociated.com was the listed website, but I could not confirm a store-specific page; Facebook page is facebook.com/Associatedfreshmarket. Only 10 Yelp reviews found, no concrete review quotes to cite.

stores.name: Marlow & Daughters

sentiments.text: Reviewers praise the quality of the cuts and describe the staff as knowledgeable and helpful.

stores.notes: 4.6/5 on Yelp from ~95 reviews. Sister business to Marlow & Sons / She Wolf Bakery, part of the same restaurant group as Diner.

stores.name: Landau's Supermarket
stores.notes: No official store website found. Large kosher supermarket per directory listings; hours Sun-Thu 6am-11pm, Fri 6am-4pm (closed for Shabbat), owner listed as Joseph Landau. No concrete review quotes surfaced.

stores.name: Prestige Organic Market
stores.notes: Opened 2021 in the Greenpoint Landing / Blue Slip waterfront development. Rating found was low (2.9 stars from only ~10 reviews) with no specific quotable review text surfaced — worth a closer look before publishing to confirm it's still operating well.

stores.name: Riverside Market
stores.notes: OSM address (7 Blue Slip) confirmed correct. Opened 2020 in the Greenpoint Landing waterfront development, ~1,500 sq ft, serves both the public and residents. No concrete review quotes found worth citing.

stores.name: Anibal Meats Market

sentiments.text: Called a neighborhood icon in the Moore Street Retail Market area, revered for its meats and its institutional-size rotisserie oven; one review called it the best, freshest meat in the neighborhood.

stores.notes: A fixture since 1967, per Edible Brooklyn — the last operating meat market on a stretch of the Moore Street Retail Market that once had several. Business is also listed under the names 'GSE Meat Market Inc' and 'Anabelle's Meat Market' in some directories; no official website found.

stores.name: Foodtown

sentiments.text: One reviewer said the store is absurdly overpriced, to the point produce isn't weighed so you can't tell what you're paying.

stores.notes: This location is operated by the same ownership group as Brooklyn Harvest Markets (formerly branded Brooklyn Harvest before converting to Foodtown around 2023) — a separate store from 'Brooklyn Harvest Market' at 25 N 5th St in this same batch. The given store-page URL returned a 404 when fetched directly; the store's continued operation is otherwise confirmed via DoorDash, Uber Eats, and directory listings.

stores.name: Bo Bo Poultry Market Inc
stores.notes: Address confirmed via USDA FSIS establishment listing and multiple directory listings (Yelp, Yellow Pages), which consistently place it at 1131 Grand St. No official website found (a similarly named 'bobo.farm' site appears to be a different, unrelated business). No concrete review text or specialty details beyond 'poultry market' could be confirmed, so specialtyItems is limited to that.

stores.name: Wize Organic Market

sentiments.text: Reviewers describe the staff as consistently friendly, with a well-curated selection and solid sandwiches.
Some customers feel the products are overpriced.

stores.notes: OSM listed no address; confirmed as 505 Union Ave via Yelp, Birdeye, and the store's own site. Yelp categorizes it partly as a sandwich shop/deli.

stores.name: Trader Joe's
bestBuys: Cut flowers and potted plants, noted by reviewers as significantly cheaper than other stores in the area

sentiments.text: Reviewers say checkout lines move quickly even when busy, with friendly, efficient clerks.
One reviewer noted the underground parking is a real convenience compared to other nearby stores.

stores.name: Ten Ichi Mart
bestBuys: 50% off sushi, onigiri, poke bowls, and all hot foods after 8pm every day

sentiments.text: One reviewer called it one of their favorite Japanese grocery stores, describing a trip there as "an EXPERIENCE."
Reviewers praise the sushi line for staying fresh and moving efficiently even with long queues.

stores.notes: Note there is a separate, differently-located Ten Ichi Mart on Smith St (Boerum Hill) — this entry is specifically the Berry St / Williamsburg location.

stores.name: Jubilee Marketplace
bestBuys: $10/lb hot bar spread including galbi, spicy tteokbokki, and stewed squid

sentiments.text: Described as a Korean grocery with a killer hot bar that feeds the neighborhood's construction crews at lunch.
Reviewers say the store is clean, well organized, and everything looks fresh.

stores.notes: No official standalone website found beyond delivery-platform pages (Grubhub, Seamless) and directory/press listings; website key omitted.

stores.name: Beyond Natural Market

sentiments.text: One reviewer called it a fantastic grocery store that leans healthy, 'kind of like a mini Whole Foods.'
Another review from October 2024 called it extremely expensive for a neighborhood supermarket.

stores.notes: OSM listed the address as 195 Montrose Ave; multiple sources (Yelp, the store's own site, Grubhub, Seamless) consistently give 199 Montrose Ave, which is used here.

stores.name: Food Expo
specialtyItems: general grocery (produce, dairy & eggs, meat & poultry, fish, bakery, deli)

sentiments.text: A short Yelp review mentions excellent customer service and good delivery service.

stores.notes: Thin data overall — small independent grocery/convenience store established around 2008, no official website found, and very few reviews (Yelp listing showed a 'last updated May 2024' timestamp, which may indicate limited recent activity, though nothing found explicitly confirms it's closed). Worth a manual double-check before publishing.

stores.name: Bravo
bestBuys: Store-made guacamole, called out by reviewers as excellent and cheap
Soy milk priced at $3.99, cited by a reviewer as a good deal

sentiments.text: Reviewers describe the store as recently renovated, clean, with quick, friendly employees.
Some reviewers complain that many items lack visible prices and that they're rung up inconsistently at checkout.

stores.notes: Family-owned since 2012 per reviews; Yelp rating is a mixed 3.0 from 22 reviews.

stores.name: Model T Meats Corporation

sentiments.text: Reviewers say the shop is immaculately clean for a butcher shop and recommend it over Whole Foods or Costco for meat.
The owner is described as very accommodating — offering free bones on request and trimming meat before weighing it.

stores.notes: No official website found; address confirmed via multiple directory sources (Yelp, Waze, Corner, Yellow Pages).

stores.name: Brooklyn Harvest Market

sentiments.text: Reviewers frequently mention friendly, accommodating staff and a visually appealing layout with a wide range of fresh produce and prepared items.
Some reviews cite expired items and unhelpful staff on a bad visit.

stores.notes: Distinct location from the 'Foodtown' store at 781 Metropolitan Ave in this same batch, though both appear to be part of the same ownership family (Brooklyn Harvest Markets).

stores.name: Lidl
bestBuys: 49-cent butter croissants baked fresh daily, part of Lidl's rotating bakery program

sentiments.text: An early reviewer described it as a very practical option for both small and larger grocery runs.

stores.notes: IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the OSM record's address ('408 Grand Street') and website (locations for store US01590) actually correspond to Lidl's Manhattan Lower East Side location (408 Grand St, NY 10002), not a Brooklyn store — confirmed by directly fetching that store's page. The OSM lat/lon (40.7116, -73.9541), however, matches Grand Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. Lidl's own press materials confirm a new Williamsburg, Brooklyn store opened August 26, 2026 at 573 Grand Street — that address is used here instead, but I could not find/confirm a store-specific lidl.com URL for it yet (it may not be indexed since it opened only days ago), so the general Lidl homepage is used for 'website' and the general offers/leaflets page for 'flyerUrl.' Given how recent this is, it's worth re-verifying the exact address once the store settles into local listings.

stores.name: Nassau Meat Market

sentiments.text: Often cited as the best Polish meat market in Greenpoint, known for its cold cuts, cheeses, and ready-made Polish dishes.

stores.notes: Also known locally as 'W Nassau Meat Market' or 'Nassau Meat Market Kiszka' across different listings — same store at this address, rated 4.7/5 across ~141 reviews.

sentiments.text: One reviewer called it a decent-size grocer for the area but warned to watch for old product and inconsistent management.
Other reviewers say it's improved recently, with aligned registers, produce misters, and a decent deli counter.

stores.name: City Fresh Market

sentiments.text: A reviewer said they found fresh products and everything they needed there.
Knishes from the bakery/deli section are praised as fresh, big, and well stuffed with potato.
One reviewer was disappointed by spoiled meat and high prices.

stores.notes: Some review aggregator pages for 'City Fresh Market' actually reference a different location (229 Knickerbocker Ave / Bushwick) — this entry is specifically the 57 Kingsland Ave / Greenpoint store.

stores.name: Steve's Food Market
bestBuys: Filet mignon noted by a reviewer as $10/lb, called the best price on cuts of steak around

sentiments.text: Described by a reviewer as the absolute best Polish deli in Greenpoint.
One reviewer said the food was good but the service was hit or miss.

stores.notes: IMPORTANT: Yelp lists a 'Steve's Meat Market' at this address as CLOSED, with a separate, currently-active listing called 'Steve's Food Market' at the same 104 Nassau Ave address (an Instagram post from around 2020 announces 'Steve's Food Market (104 Nassau Ave.) is now open'). This looks like a rebrand/successor of the original butcher shop into a broader deli/food market at the same spot, not a still-operating business under the exact OSM name. No official website found for either name. Worth confirming current name/signage before publishing.
